observation.visible_scene: A close-up, fixed view of a dark non-stick pan. Near the center sits a small square pat of pale, solid butter, partially surrounded by a pool of already-melted, yellowish butter whose edges are ringed with white foam and bubbles. Scattered droplets (oil or moisture) dot the pan surface, and a soft blurred highlight runs along the out-of-focus far rim of the pan.
visible_changes: The solid butter pat stays in the same central position throughout; it does not translate, and it does not disappear within the excerpt.

The pat's shape slowly softens: its corners/edges look marginally more rounded and less crisp toward the later frames, consistent with continued melting at the boundary, while the bulk remains intact.

The surrounding melted pool keeps roughly the same overall extent; its foam/bubble pattern continuously shifts (bubbles appearing, popping, and re-forming along the rim), indicating ongoing simmering rather than a single event.

The background pan surface, the scattered droplets, the rim highlight, and the dark out-of-focus blob at the top remain fixed in position, so the camera is static and the changes are physical (melting/foaming), not viewpoint changes.
outside_clip_unknowns: When the butter was placed in the pan and the heat level applied (the melting pool already exists at the first frame, so the onset is before this excerpt).
Whether the pat eventually melts completely and what happens after the last frame.
uncertain_details: Whether the melted pool's radius grows slightly or stays effectively constant is hard to judge against the shifting foam.
The exact material of the surface droplets (oil vs. water) is not determinable from the frames.
